name: Beeswax
source: Illustrative bulk elemental composition of beeswax (predominantly long-chain wax esters and hydrocarbons): C ~79.6%, H ~13.44%, O ~6.46%, trace pollen/propolis ash ~0.5% (wax chemistry literature).
notes: Beeswax is markedly more reduced (far lower oxygen content) than a triglyceride fat or a carbohydrate, consistent with real wax-ester and long-chain-hydrocarbon chemistry rather than the generic "fat" conversion factor used elsewhere in this dataset. origin/honey.ts sources wax from honey consumed by the hive via splitByProfile against this profile and a respiration-product ("spent" CO2+H2O) stream, following the widely cited beekeeping figure that bees consume roughly six to eight kilograms of honey per kilogram of wax secreted.
